alignments.note: Corrected. The ASV renders the relative and the generalizing particle by the single English word whoso, so the pair is one aligned unit under rule 39's test and the count test rule 50 states, headed on the relative: part of the word — the -so — answers to the particle exactly as a -soever does, and rule 72's compressed arm follows rule 50 in terms. Rule 72's unrepresented arm reaches only a pair for which the ASV writes a separate word for the relative and none for the particle, as οὗ ἐάν → that does at 18:19. MAT.18.6's identical Ὃς ἄν → whoso is what shows this is the chapter's analysis (rule 24), and unit SBLGNT.MAT.18.5.v002 leaves ἄν itself compatible with the projection here. Leaving the particle unrepresented remains the reading a strict -soever test would give.
Child glosses the lexeme, little renders the diminutive (rule 66).
The genitive pronoun writes the possessive my, displacing the article's determiner (rule 20).

review_notes: Corrected the ὃς ἐάν pair to a single aligned unit on whoso, so that the chapter analyses 18:5 and 18:6 alike where the ASV writes the same English for the same construction (rule 24). The accepted unit read rule 72's unrepresented arm off the absence of a -soever, which rule 50 says in terms is the ordinary case and not the test.

Units SBLGNT.MAT.18.5.v002 and v003 remain underdetermined; the projection's readings are all translated by the ASV, so no textual note is owed. v002 covers ἐάν itself and leaves ἄν compatible, which is a further reason 18:5 and 18:6 should not turn on the lexeme.
A reference comparison will now report ἐάν here as represented; that agreement with BSB is a consequence of the correction and not its reason.
